issues.description: Method acceptSupplyDelivery: the problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies a four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). The provided implementation and example call sites use a three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (omitting the supplier parameter and using a single ambiguous 'name' parameter). This mismatch affects the method signature (parameter count and meaning) and will cause compilation or test invocation errors and confusion for students implementing the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to declare acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and remove the supplier parameter from the UML/text, or (B) update the template and solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and adjust all call sites (e.g., Main) and tests accordingly. Ensure parameter names in the signature are descriptive (supplierName, ingredientName, price, quantity) and that call sites use the same argument order.

issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock: the problem statement contains contradictory instructions. One paragraph instructs students to initialize the stock field in the constructor (implying an instance field), while a later note explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across instances. The reference implementation declares stock as a static final field (private static final Stock stock = new Stock();). This inconsistency will confuse students about whether to declare stock as an instance or a static field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement: explicitly state whether stock is a static (shared) field or an instance field. If the intended design is shared stock, update the earlier constructor initialization instruction to indicate that stock should be declared as a static final field (e.g., private static final Stock stock = new Stock();) or initialized in a static initializer. If the intended design is an instance field, remove the 'static' requirement and adjust the reference solution and any tests accordingly. Make the statement consistent across the UML, textual description, and examples.
